outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a pressure-measuring device designed to convert mechanical or hydraulic pressure into a measuring signal that can be transmitted to a remote evaluation unit. The device is particularly suitable for use in connection with machines such as motors or pumps, where pressure conditions must be monitored reliably and, if necessary, from a distance.

The pressure-measuring device includes a fastening device by means of which it can be attached to the machine housing of a motor, pump, or similar unit. This fastening device allows the measuring device to be securely mounted at the location where the pressure to be detected occurs, ensuring accurate transfer of the pressure force to the measuring mechanism.

A transmitter head is arranged on the measuring device head. This transmitter head is connected to a light source by a first optical fiber, so that light generated by the light source can be guided to the transmitter head. Opposite the transmitter head, a receiver head is mounted in such a way that a light path is formed between the transmitter head and the receiver head. The receiver head receives light transmitted across this light path and is connected to the remote evaluation unit by a second optical fiber.

The device further comprises a measuring element that responds to mechanical or hydraulic pressure. When such pressure is applied, the measuring element moves into the light path between the transmitter head and the receiver head. This movement changes the amount or characteristics of the light received by the receiver head. The resulting optical change is transmitted through the second optical fiber to the evaluation unit, where it is converted into a measuring signal representative of the applied pressure.

In this manner, the pressure-measuring device provides an optical means of detecting pressure and transmitting the corresponding measurement signal to a remote location. Since the signal transmission is carried out by optical fibers, the device is well suited for applications in which electrical interference, harsh environments, or spatial separation between the measuring point and the evaluation unit must be taken into account.
outputs.L4:
A pressure-measuring device is provided for detecting mechanical or hydraulic pressure occurring in a motor housing, pump housing, or similar machine component and for converting that pressure into a measuring signal that can be evaluated at a remote location. The device includes a fastening or mounting arrangement by which it can be secured to the housing whose internal pressure is to be monitored. Connected to the fastening arrangement are an optical transmitter head and an optical receiver head, which are coupled respectively to optical fibers for transmitting light to and from a remote evaluation unit.

During operation, light is guided through an optical fiber to the transmitter head, from which it is directed across a defined light path toward the receiver head. The receiver head collects the transmitted light and guides it through a further optical fiber to an evaluating device. A pressure-sensitive or pressure-displaceable measuring element is arranged so that it can move in response to the pressure acting in the housing. As the pressure changes, the measuring element is displaced and enters the optical path between the transmitter head and the receiver head to a greater or lesser extent.

This displacement changes the amount, intensity, or distribution of light received by the receiver head. The resulting variation in the optical signal is transmitted through the receiver-side optical fiber to the remote evaluation unit, where it is interpreted as a measure of the pressure acting on the measuring element. In this way, pressure can be measured without requiring electrical components at the measuring point, which is advantageous in environments subject to vibration, electromagnetic interference, explosive atmospheres, high humidity, or other harsh operating conditions.

The device therefore enables reliable remote optical pressure measurement in motors, pumps, and comparable technical systems. By converting pressure-induced movement directly into a change in a light signal, the arrangement provides a simple, robust, and electrically isolated means of monitoring pressure conditions within a housing or pressure chamber.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it plays an important role in communication. It is called a definite article, and it helps us point to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we are talking about a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word gives sentences clarity and direction. It can refer to something already mentioned, something unique, or something understood from context. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our everyday experience. We say “the door” when both people know which door is being discussed.

Although “the” may seem ordinary, it is essential to English. Without it, many sentences would sound unnatural or unclear. Its quiet presence helps organize meaning, connect ideas, and make language more precise. In this way, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a pressure-measuring device that uses optical fibers, with a transmitter head and receiver head on a measuring device head and a pressure-displaceable element interrupting the light path.
counterfactuals.output: An optical pressure-measuring device comprises a measuring device head carrying an optical transmitter head and an optical receiver head arranged with a light path extending therebetween. The transmitter head and receiver head are respectively coupled to optical fibers for transmitting emitted light to the measuring device head and returning received light from the measuring device head to an evaluation unit. A pressure-responsive, displaceable element is disposed in the region of the light path and is movable as a function of an applied pressure between positions in which it variably interrupts, attenuates, or permits optical transmission between the transmitter head and the receiver head. The resulting change in received light intensity is representative of the pressure acting on the displaceable element and may be converted into a pressure value by the evaluation unit. The device provides electrical isolation at the measuring location and is suitable for pressure measurement in electromagnetically sensitive, explosive, or otherwise hazardous environments.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for converting mechanical or hydraulic pressure into a measurement signal sent to a remote evaluation unit, including fastening to a motor or pump housing and optical fiber connections.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention relates to a pressure-measuring device for converting mechanical or hydraulic pressure into a measurement signal that can be transmitted to a remote evaluation unit, preferably by optical means.

The device comprises a pressure sensor unit that is arranged directly on, in, or adjacent to a component subjected to pressure, such as a motor housing, pump housing, valve block, hydraulic cylinder, or pressure line. The sensor unit includes a pressure-sensitive element, for example a diaphragm, membrane, piston, strain body, or deformable measuring element, which is acted upon by the mechanical or hydraulic pressure to be measured. The deformation, displacement, or stress produced in this element is converted into an optical measurement signal.

For this purpose, the pressure-sensitive element is coupled to at least one optical fiber. The optical fiber may include a fiber Bragg grating, an interferometric measuring section, a reflective end face, or another optically detectable sensing structure. When pressure is applied, the optical properties of the fiber or sensing structure change, for example by a shift in reflected wavelength, a change in intensity, phase shift, polarization change, or optical path length variation. This optical change represents the measured pressure.

The sensor unit is fastened to the motor or pump housing by a mechanical fastening arrangement, such as a threaded connection, flange, clamp, screw connection, bayonet fitting, or press-fit mount. A sealing element, for example an O-ring, gasket, metal seal, or bonded sealing layer, may be provided between the sensor unit and the housing so that hydraulic fluid or process medium cannot escape. The fastening arrangement may be designed so that the sensor can be mounted in an existing pressure port, inspection opening, drain bore, lubrication channel, or specially formed receiving bore of the housing.

The optical fiber connection is routed from the sensor unit to a remote evaluation unit. The fiber may be protected by a sheath, strain relief element, armored cable, conduit, or connector housing to withstand vibration, temperature changes, oil, moisture, and mechanical stress. The sensor unit may include an optical connector, splice connection, ferrule, or sealed feedthrough for coupling the internal sensing fiber to an external optical fiber cable.

The remote evaluation unit contains an optical transmitter, receiver, interrogator, or light source and detector arrangement. It sends light through the optical fiber to the sensor and receives the modified optical signal returning from or passing through the sensor. The evaluation unit processes the optical signal and determines the corresponding pressure value. The resulting pressure measurement may be displayed, stored, transmitted to a control system, or used for monitoring and regulating operation of the motor, pump, or hydraulic system.

Because the measurement signal is transmitted optically, the system is insensitive to electromagnetic interference and can be used in electrically noisy environments, such as near electric motors, frequency converters, pumps, compressors, turbines, or heavy industrial machinery. The invention also permits the evaluation electronics to be positioned remotely from heat, vibration, oil, or hazardous areas, while the compact sensor unit remains mounted directly at the pressure source.

In one embodiment, the pressure-sensitive diaphragm is integrated into a threaded plug that is screwed into a pump housing. An optical fiber with a fiber Bragg grating is bonded to or embedded in the diaphragm. Hydraulic pressure inside the pump deflects the diaphragm, straining the grating and shifting its reflected wavelength. The reflected wavelength is transmitted through the optical fiber to the remote evaluation unit, which calculates the pressure.

In another embodiment, the sensor is mounted externally on a motor or pump housing and detects pressure-induced deformation of the housing wall. A clamping or screw-mounted sensor body presses an optical strain-sensing fiber against the housing surface. Changes in housing deformation caused by internal pressure are detected optically and evaluated remotely.

The invention therefore provides a robust pressure-measuring arrangement in which mechanical or hydraulic pressure is converted into an optical measurement signal at the measuring location and transmitted via optical fiber to a remote evaluation unit, with reliable mechanical fastening to a motor or pump housing.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a European patent claim summary for a pressure sensor with a fastening device, transmitter head, receiver head, first and second optical fibers, and a measuring element movable into the light path under pressure.
counterfactuals.output:
**Claim Summary (European Patent Style)**

1. **A pressure sensor** comprising:  
   - a **fastening device** configured to secure the pressure sensor to a pressure-carrying component;  
   - a **transmitter head** arranged on or in the fastening device;  
   - a **receiver head** arranged opposite or offset from the transmitter head;  
   - a **first optical fiber** optically coupled to the transmitter head for guiding light to the transmitter head;  
   - a **second optical fiber** optically coupled to the receiver head for guiding received light away from the receiver head; and  
   - a **measuring element** arranged between the transmitter head and the receiver head,  

   wherein the transmitter head is configured to emit light into a light path toward the receiver head, and wherein the measuring element is movable, in response to pressure acting on the pressure sensor, into the light path so as to alter the light received by the receiver head.

2. The pressure sensor according to claim 1, wherein the measuring element is displaced proportionally to an applied pressure, thereby varying an optical signal transmitted from the transmitter head to the receiver head.

3. The pressure sensor according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the measuring element is configured to partially or completely interrupt, attenuate, reflect, refract, or scatter the light in the light path.

4. The pressure sensor according to any preceding claim, wherein the fastening device comprises a threaded portion, flange, clamp, or sealing surface for mounting the pressure sensor to a vessel, pipe, housing, or process connection.

5. The pressure sensor according to any preceding claim, wherein the measuring element is coupled to a pressure-responsive diaphragm, membrane, piston, or elastic body.

6. The pressure sensor according to any preceding claim, wherein the first and second optical fibers are arranged to transmit and receive light without electrical components being present at a pressure-exposed measuring region.

7. The pressure sensor according to any preceding claim, wherein the receiver head is configured to generate an optical output signal dependent on the position of the measuring element in the light path, the optical output signal being representative of the applied pressure.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical invention disclosure paragraph for an optically coupled pressure-measuring device mounted on a machine housing, where pressure displacement affects light transmission between opposing heads.
counterfactuals.output: An optically coupled pressure-measuring device is disclosed for mounting to a machine housing and sensing internal or external pressure without requiring an electrical pressure transducer at the pressure interface. The device includes a pressure-responsive member, such as a diaphragm, piston, or elastomeric membrane, mechanically coupled to a movable optical head positioned opposite a fixed optical head across an optical gap. One of the heads includes a light emitter or optical fiber output and the opposing head includes a light receiver or optical fiber input, such that light transmission between the heads varies as the pressure-responsive member is displaced by pressure acting on the machine housing. The displacement changes one or more optical coupling parameters, including gap distance, lateral alignment, angular alignment, beam interception, attenuation, reflection, or transmission area, thereby producing an optical signal representative of pressure. The optical heads may be sealed from the process medium by a transparent window or isolated by the pressure-responsive member, enabling operation in harsh, high-temperature, high-vibration, or electrically noisy environments. In certain embodiments, the emitted light is supplied and/or the received light is returned through optical fibers to remote electronics, which determine pressure based on calibrated changes in optical intensity, wavelength, phase, or modulation. The device may be integrated into a threaded port, flange, cover plate, or wall of the machine housing, and may include temperature compensation, reference optical paths, mechanical stops, biasing springs, and calibration features to improve accuracy and durability.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
